correctness.rationale: Differentiating the squared Euclidean norm shows contractivity for all t≥0 iff H=(J+Jᵀ)/2 is negative semidefinite. At b=a the signed cyclic shift is orthogonal with Q^n=−I, and the top symmetric eigenspace is the real cosine/sine pair at θ=π/n. Compressing the symmetric corner perturbation to this pair gives eigenvalues (cosθ+1)/n and (cosθ−1)/n, yielding the strict two-sided lower bound away from b=a. For z=μ/a>cosθ the interior path block of −H is positive definite. Its Chebyshev inverse entries give a two-dimensional complement with diagonal (a/2)U_(n−1)/U_(n−2) and off-diagonal (a/2)(b/a−1/U_(n−2)); the scalar PSD condition and b≥0 give the exact interval, including n=3. At the minimum damping only b=a works and the neutral modes are an undamped conjugate pair. The open-chain eigenvalues are −μ, but its top symmetric eigenvalue is −μ+a cos(π/(n+1)); the balanced closure has top real part −μ+a cos(π/n), giving the stated strict separation. The example reduces to U₁=6/5 and U₂=11/25. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The leading path block of size n−1 is positive definite if z>c=cos(π/n), so the determinant sign alone decides PSD by the scalar Schur complement. The identity U_(n−1)²−U_n U_(n−2)=1 converts its sign test to |β U_(n−2)−1|≤U_(n−1); restrict β≥0. Below c the same path block obstructs PSD; at z=c the determinant is −(β−1)² and the known balanced spectrum gives positivity at β=1. The projected corner on the explicit prior pair has trace 2c/n and determinant −sin²(π/n)/n², giving the two slopes by the Rayleigh bound. The stable-open/nonamplifying-closed band then just compares the usual open path eigenvalue with the balanced eigenvalue and uses the open chain's triangular spectrum.

originality.rationale: Grudsky–Maximenko–Soto-González (2020 preprint/2021 publication) treat exactly the shifted and scaled symmetric matrix, under a more general complex corner parameter. Their Proposition 1 gives the all-order Chebyshev determinant, from which the fixed-Euclidean window and unique optimizer follow by a positive path pivot and a square completion. Their Proposition 12 gives the precise double extremal eigenspace, whose two-by-two Rayleigh restriction gives the stated slopes. The paper need not use the ecological wording; the main claims are routine consequences of exact results for the same matrix. This is not a claim that Snyder or the secant criterion itself gives the Euclidean window.
residual_risks: Snyder's full text and the exact signed-triangle catalogue file were unavailable in the bounded attempts. This is not used to infer noncoverage, and the exact available Toeplitz theorem already settles the implication.

But here the exact window, feedback minimizer, slopes and open/closed comparison require only standard transformations of already available spectrum data for the same matrix. The frozen ecological interpretation does not supply a separate nonroutine result; no repair is warranted.
